text: Wee Engineer Units: Introductory engineering challenges for young learners using everyday materials. Units: Loud Noisemakers, Wind-Powered Fans, Wrecking Balls, Rafts.

title: Loud Noisemakers
category: YES - Preschool / Early Childhood
text: Loud Noisemakers is a Preschool / Early Childhood unit from the Museum of Science, Boston. Four unique design challenges that can be taught in any order build children's confidence in engineering. Aligned MA STE standard PreK-ETS1-1(MA) / PreK-PS2-1(MA): Ask questions, use simple materials, and explore push/pull forces to design functional physical objects. Related museum exhibits: Soundstair & Kinetic Art, AlegreMENTE | Happy Brain.

Aligned MA STE standard PreK-ETS1-1(MA) / PreK-PS2-1(MA): Ask questions, use simple materials, and explore push/pull forces to design functional physical objects. title: YES: YES Elementary (Grades K–5)
category: YES Curriculum Overview
text: Standards-aligned core engineering units structured for elementary classrooms. Units: Engineering Sun Hats, Engineering Trash Collectors, Engineering Drums, Engineering Nightlights, Engineering Pumpkin Pollinators, Engineering Magnetic Dog Doors, Engineering Plastic Filters, Engineering Safety Vests.

title: Engineering Sun Hats
category: YES - YES Elementary (Grades K–5)
text: Engineering Sun Hats is a YES Elementary (Grades K–5) unit from the Museum of Science, Boston. Students explore the cooling effects of shade as they engineer sun hats that block sunlight and meet users’ needs. Grade band: Kindergarten. Aligned MA STE standard K-PS3-2: Design and build a model structure to reduce the warming effect of sunlight on an area.

title: Engineering Trash Collectors
category: YES - YES Elementary (Grades K–5)
text: Engineering Trash Collectors is a YES Elementary (Grades K–5) unit from the Museum of Science, Boston. Students consider how materials behave in water and can be shaped as they engineer a collector to remove trash from a model pond. Grade band: Kindergarten. Aligned MA STE standard K-ESS3-3 / K-ETS1-1: Communicate solutions to reduce human impact on environment and natural resources. Related museum exhibits: Yawkey Gallery on the Charles River.

title: Engineering Drums
category: YES - YES Elementary (Grades K–5)
text: Engineering Drums is a YES Elementary (Grades K–5) unit from the Museum of Science, Boston. Students explore how different materials can be used to make different sounds as they engineer a set of drums that tells different actors when to come onstage in a play. Grade band: Lower Elementary (Grades 1–2). Aligned MA STE standard 1-PS4-1: Plan and conduct investigations to demonstrate that vibrating materials produce sound and sound causes vibration. Related museum exhibits: Soundstair & Kinetic Art.

title: Engineering Nightlights
category: YES - YES Elementary (Grades K–5)
text: Engineering Nightlights is a YES Elementary (Grades K–5) unit from the Museum of Science, Boston. Students investigate how materials interact with light as they engineer nightlights that meet user preferences and communicate a message. Grade band: Lower Elementary (Grades 1–2). Aligned MA STE standard 1-PS4-3: Plan and conduct investigations to determine the effect of placing objects made with different materials in the path of a beam of light. Related museum exhibits: Theater of Electricity.

title: Engineering Pumpkin Pollinators
category: YES - YES Elementary (Grades K–5)
text: Engineering Pumpkin Pollinators is a YES Elementary (Grades K–5) unit from the Museum of Science, Boston. After learning about pollinators and their importance, students engineer hand pollinators that move pollen from one pumpkin flower to another. Grade band: Lower Elementary (Grades 1–2). Aligned MA STE standard 2-LS2-2: Develop a simple model that mimics the function of an animal in pollinating plants or dispersing seeds. Related museum exhibits: A Bird's World.

title: Engineering Magnetic Dog Doors
category: YES - YES Elementary (Grades K–5)
text: Engineering Magnetic Dog Doors is a YES Elementary (Grades K–5) unit from the Museum of Science, Boston. Students engineer dog door systems for an animal shelter that can open or stay closed using magnetic forces. Grade band: Upper Elementary (Grades 3–5). Aligned MA STE standard 3-PS2-4: Define a simple design problem that can be solved by applying scientific ideas about magnets.

title: Engineering Plastic Filters
category: YES - YES Elementary (Grades K–5)
text: Engineering Plastic Filters is a YES Elementary (Grades K–5) unit from the Museum of Science, Boston. Students consider the effects of plastics on the marine ecosystem and community as they engineer filters to reduce plastic waste entering the ocean. Grade band: Upper Elementary (Grades 3–5). Aligned MA STE standard 5-ESS3-1 / 3-5-ETS1-2: Evaluate individual and community solutions to protect Earth’s resources and environment through filtration systems. Related museum exhibits: Yawkey Gallery on the Charles River, Nanotechnology.

title: Engineering Safety Vests
category: YES - YES Elementary (Grades K–5)
text: Engineering Safety Vests is a YES Elementary (Grades K–5) unit from the Museum of Science, Boston. Students engineer vests that incorporate an electric communication system to increase users' safety in a busy intersection. Grade band: Upper Elementary (Grades 3–5). Aligned MA STE standard 4-PS4-2 / 3-5-ETS1-1: Develop a model to describe that light reflecting from objects into the eye allows objects to be seen, testing high-visibility safety materials.

title: YES: YES Middle School (Grades 6–8)
category: YES Curriculum Overview
text: Real-world engineering challenges designed for middle school students, incorporating integrated computer science options. Units: Engineering Earthquake-Resistant Buildings, Engineering Eco-friendly Slippers, Engineering Landing Pads, Engineering Medicine Coolers, Engineering Vision Extenders, Engineering Wearable Alerts.

title: Engineering Earthquake-Resistant Buildings
category: YES - YES Middle School (Grades 6–8)
text: Engineering Earthquake-Resistant Buildings is a YES Middle School (Grades 6–8) unit from the Museum of Science, Boston. Students explore how earthquakes damage buildings and engineer a model building that can experience an earthquake without deforming. Aligned MA STE standard MS-ETS1-2 / MS-ESS3-2: Evaluate structural solutions using shake tables to mitigate natural hazard impacts on human-built environments. Related museum exhibits: Engineering Design Workshop.

title: Engineering Eco-friendly Slippers
category: YES - YES Middle School (Grades 6–8)
text: Engineering Eco-friendly Slippers is a YES Middle School (Grades 6–8) unit from the Museum of Science, Boston. Students investigate balanced and unbalanced forces with a focus on friction as they engineer an eco-friendly slipper with a safe amount of traction. Aligned MA STE standard MS-ETS1-1 / MS-ESS3-4: Design solutions to minimize human environmental impact by selecting renewable, sustainable materials. Related museum exhibits: Innovation: Earth.

title: Engineering Landing Pads
category: YES - YES Middle School (Grades 6–8)
text: Engineering Landing Pads is a YES Middle School (Grades 6–8) unit from the Museum of Science, Boston. Students prepare for the future of drone deliveries by engineering a cushioned landing pad that absorbs kinetic energy during a collision with a dropped item. Aligned MA STE standard MS-ETS1-2 / MS-PS2-2: Apply Newton's laws of motion to design shock-absorbing landing mechanics that reduce collision force. Related museum exhibits: To the Moon.

title: Engineering Medicine Coolers
category: YES - YES Middle School (Grades 6–8)
text: Engineering Medicine Coolers is a YES Middle School (Grades 6–8) unit from the Museum of Science, Boston. Students explore heat transfer as they engineer chemical cold packs and insulation for a container that keeps medicine cool. Aligned MA STE standard MS-ETS1-3 / MS-PS3-3: Apply scientific principles of thermal energy transfer to design, construct, and test thermal insulation devices.

title: Engineering Vision Extenders
category: YES - YES Middle School (Grades 6–8)
text: Engineering Vision Extenders is a YES Middle School (Grades 6–8) unit from the Museum of Science, Boston. Students use what they learn about the reflection of light as they engineer devices that extend users’ vision behind them. Aligned MA STE standard MS-ETS1-2 / MS-PS4-2: Construct optical reflection and refraction models to extend visual capabilities. Related museum exhibits: The Art of Illusion, Take a Closer Look.

title: Engineering Wearable Alerts
category: YES - YES Middle School (Grades 6–8)
text: Engineering Wearable Alerts is a YES Middle School (Grades 6–8) unit from the Museum of Science, Boston. Students investigate circuits, switches, and systems as they engineer a wearable technology that signals when the user is in “text neck” position. Aligned MA STE standard MS-ETS1-1 / MS-CS-1: Program microcontrollers and sensors to create wearable bio-monitoring or safety devices.

title: YES: YES Enrichment (Out-of-School & Electives)
category: YES Curriculum Overview
text: Units designed specifically for afterschool programs, summer camps, and STEM electives. Units: Engineering Antivirals, Engineering Bandages, Engineering Bubble Wands, Engineering Parachutes, Engineering Rescue Shuttles, Engineering Sails, Engineering Sock Assistive Devices, Engineering Upcycled Toy Vehicles, Engineering an Avalanche Protection System (Engineering Adventures), Engineering Vertical Farms (Engineering Everywhere).

title: Engineering Antivirals
category: YES - YES Enrichment (Out-of-School & Electives)
text: Engineering Antivirals is a YES Enrichment (Out-of-School & Electives) unit from the Museum of Science, Boston. Youth engineer a model antiviral to stop a virus from attaching to a cell. Aligned MA STE standard MS-ETS1-2 / MS-LS1-1: Design physical and biological barrier solutions to protect living systems against pathogen transmission. Related museum exhibits: Hall of Human Life, Nanotechnology.

title: Engineering Bandages
category: YES - YES Enrichment (Out-of-School & Electives)
text: Engineering Bandages is a YES Enrichment (Out-of-School & Electives) unit from the Museum of Science, Boston. Youth engineer bandages that can cover and protect a model cut. Aligned MA STE standard MS-ETS1-2 / MS-LS1-1: Design physical and biological barrier solutions to protect living systems against pathogen transmission. Related museum exhibits: Hall of Human Life.

title: Engineering Bubble Wands
category: YES - YES Enrichment (Out-of-School & Electives)
text: Engineering Bubble Wands is a YES Enrichment (Out-of-School & Electives) unit from the Museum of Science, Boston. Youth engineer bubble wands to make a variety of bubbles.

title: Engineering Parachutes
category: YES - YES Enrichment (Out-of-School & Electives)
text: Engineering Parachutes is a YES Enrichment (Out-of-School & Electives) unit from the Museum of Science, Boston. Youth engineer a parachute that falls slowly to deliver seeds. Aligned MA STE standard 3-5-ETS1-2 / MS-PS2-2: Evaluate drag force, surface area, and fluid resistance in transportation prototypes. Related museum exhibits: Science in the Park.

title: Engineering Rescue Shuttles
category: YES - YES Enrichment (Out-of-School & Electives)
text: Engineering Rescue Shuttles is a YES Enrichment (Out-of-School & Electives) unit from the Museum of Science, Boston. Youth design a shuttle to land a rope near a person who needs a rescue. Aligned MA STE standard(s) via related exhibits: MS-ESS1-2. Related museum exhibits: To the Moon.

title: Engineering Sails
category: YES - YES Enrichment (Out-of-School & Electives)
text: Engineering Sails is a YES Enrichment (Out-of-School & Electives) unit from the Museum of Science, Boston. Youth engineer a sail that catches wind energy to move a vehicle across a distance. Aligned MA STE standard 3-5-ETS1-2 / MS-PS2-2: Evaluate drag force, surface area, and fluid resistance in transportation prototypes.

title: Engineering Sock Assistive Devices
category: YES - YES Enrichment (Out-of-School & Electives)
text: Engineering Sock Assistive Devices is a YES Enrichment (Out-of-School & Electives) unit from the Museum of Science, Boston. Youth engineer an assistive device that helps people with limited mobility put on their socks.

title: Engineering Upcycled Toy Vehicles
category: YES - YES Enrichment (Out-of-School & Electives)
text: Engineering Upcycled Toy Vehicles is a YES Enrichment (Out-of-School & Electives) unit from the Museum of Science, Boston. Youth engineer a toy vehicle using upcycled materials. Aligned MA STE standard(s) via related exhibits: 3-5-ETS1-2. Related museum exhibits: Machines & Transportation.

title: Engineering an Avalanche Protection System (Engineering Adventures)
category: YES - YES Enrichment (Out-of-School & Electives)
text: Engineering an Avalanche Protection System (Engineering Adventures) is a YES Enrichment (Out-of-School & Electives) unit from the Museum of Science, Boston. Kids design a system to hold or divert massive amounts of snow away from a town. Aligned MA STE standard(s) via related exhibits: MS-ESS3-2. Related museum exhibits: Arctic Adventure: Exploring with Technology.

title: Engineering Vertical Farms (Engineering Everywhere)
category: YES - YES Enrichment (Out-of-School & Electives)
text: Engineering Vertical Farms (Engineering Everywhere) is a YES Enrichment (Out-of-School & Electives) unit from the Museum of Science, Boston. Students design a vertical farm to increase the amount of food that can be grown in a small space. Aligned MA STE standard MS-ESS3-3 / MS-ETS1-2: Construct agricultural technologies that optimize land, water, and nutrient usage in urban environments. Related museum exhibits: Innovation: Earth.

title: YES: YES STEM Event Activities
category: YES Curriculum Overview
text: Quick 10–20 minute family and community engineering activities. Units: Engineering a Park Cleanup, Engineering a Seed Spreader, Engineering a Toy Rescue.

title: Engineering a Park Cleanup
category: YES - YES STEM Event Activities
text: Engineering a Park Cleanup is a YES STEM Event Activities unit from the Museum of Science, Boston. Groups engineer a solution to safely clean up picnic items carried away by the wind. Aligned MA STE standard K-5-ETS1-1: Define criteria and constraints for rapid 10–20 minute design challenges solving community problems.

title: Engineering a Seed Spreader
category: YES - YES STEM Event Activities
text: Engineering a Seed Spreader is a YES STEM Event Activities unit from the Museum of Science, Boston. Groups engineer a solution to scatter seeds across bare spots in a garden. Aligned MA STE standard K-5-ETS1-1: Define criteria and constraints for rapid 10–20 minute design challenges solving community problems.

title: Engineering a Toy Rescue
category: YES - YES STEM Event Activities
text: Engineering a Toy Rescue is a YES STEM Event Activities unit from the Museum of Science, Boston. Groups engineer a solution to safely rescue a toy drone from a tree. Aligned MA STE standard K-5-ETS1-1: Define criteria and constraints for rapid 10–20 minute design challenges solving community problems.

title: YES: Middle School Computer Science Companion Modules
category: YES Curriculum Overview
text: Integrated computer science and data analysis modules designed to accompany YES engineering units. Units: Alert Simulations, Bounce Height Measurements, Delivery Notification Systems, Exoplanet Discoveries, Heatwave Visualizations, Light Sensors, Medicine Cooler Alarms, Photo Classification, Signal Bracelets, Step Counters, Text Neck Timers, User Reviews Analysis.

title: Alert Simulations
category: YES - Middle School Computer Science Companion Modules
text: Alert Simulations is a Middle School Computer Science Companion Modules unit from the Museum of Science, Boston. Students use simulations to refine the timing and duration of a wearable alert algorithm.

title: Bounce Height Measurements
category: YES - Middle School Computer Science Companion Modules
text: Bounce Height Measurements is a Middle School Computer Science Companion Modules unit from the Museum of Science, Boston. Students use a computer to collect precise data on how high a ping pong ball bounces on different landing materials. Aligned MA STE standard(s) via related exhibits: MS-CS-2, MS-ETS1-7(MA). Related museum exhibits: Mathematica: A World of Numbers, Math Moves!: Ratio & Proportion.

title: Delivery Notification Systems
category: YES - Middle School Computer Science Companion Modules
text: Delivery Notification Systems is a Middle School Computer Science Companion Modules unit from the Museum of Science, Boston. Students design a delivery notification system to alert them when urgent items are delivered to a landing pad.

title: Exoplanet Discoveries
category: YES - Middle School Computer Science Companion Modules
text: Exoplanet Discoveries is a Middle School Computer Science Companion Modules unit from the Museum of Science, Boston. Students explore how computer algorithms can be written to search Kepler Space Telescope data for evidence of exoplanets. Aligned MA STE standard(s) via related exhibits: MS-ESS1-1. Related museum exhibits: Charles Hayden Planetarium / Cosmic Light.

title: Heatwave Visualizations
category: YES - Middle School Computer Science Companion Modules
text: Heatwave Visualizations is a Middle School Computer Science Companion Modules unit from the Museum of Science, Boston. Students visualize heatwave data to identify who could benefit most from a medicine cooler. Aligned MA STE standard MS-CS-1 / MS-CS-2: Design algorithms, process sensor input data, and analyze environmental trends using computational tools. Related museum exhibits: Gaia Globe.

title: Light Sensors
category: YES - Middle School Computer Science Companion Modules
text: Light Sensors is a Middle School Computer Science Companion Modules unit from the Museum of Science, Boston. Students use micro:bits and MakeCode to design and build a simple light sensor. Aligned MA STE standard MS-CS-1 / MS-CS-2: Design algorithms, process sensor input data, and analyze environmental trends using computational tools. Related museum exhibits: Theater of Electricity.

title: Medicine Cooler Alarms
category: YES - Middle School Computer Science Companion Modules
text: Medicine Cooler Alarms is a Middle School Computer Science Companion Modules unit from the Museum of Science, Boston. Students write an algorithm for a micro:bit that continuously monitors temperature and sounds an alarm when a medicine cooler gets too warm.

title: Photo Classification
category: YES - Middle School Computer Science Companion Modules
text: Photo Classification is a Middle School Computer Science Companion Modules unit from the Museum of Science, Boston. Students train and test an online photo classification model to distinguish between photos of animals and photos of trash. Aligned MA STE standard(s) via related exhibits: MS-CS-1. Related museum exhibits: Exploring AI: Making the Invisible Visible.

title: Signal Bracelets
category: YES - Middle School Computer Science Companion Modules
text: Signal Bracelets is a Middle School Computer Science Companion Modules unit from the Museum of Science, Boston. Students use MakeCode and micro:bits to design a signal bracelet that displays signals when activated by kinesthetic inputs.

title: Step Counters
category: YES - Middle School Computer Science Companion Modules
text: Step Counters is a Middle School Computer Science Companion Modules unit from the Museum of Science, Boston. Students use a micro:bit's accelerometer and concepts such as loops, conditionals, and variables to develop a step counting algorithm in MakeCode. Aligned MA STE standard MS-CS-1 / MS-CS-2: Design algorithms, process sensor input data, and analyze environmental trends using computational tools.

title: Text Neck Timers
category: YES - Middle School Computer Science Companion Modules
text: Text Neck Timers is a Middle School Computer Science Companion Modules unit from the Museum of Science, Boston. Students use MakeCode and micro:bits to design a timer that alerts a user when they have been in text neck position for too long. Aligned MA STE standard MS-CS-1 / MS-CS-2: Design algorithms, process sensor input data, and analyze environmental trends using computational tools.

title: User Reviews Analysis
category: YES - Middle School Computer Science Companion Modules
text: User Reviews Analysis is a Middle School Computer Science Companion Modules unit from the Museum of Science, Boston. Students train a computer to analyze slipper user reviews and investigate how adjusting the training data impacts the machine learning model's accuracy.

title: YES: EiE (Engineering is Elementary) Units
category: YES Curriculum Overview
text: Narrative-based design challenges developed by EiE at the Museum of Science. Units: EiE Kindergarten: Programming Robots to Recycle, Designing Plant Packages, Designing Solar Ovens, Designing Windmills, Evaluating a Landscape, Improving a Play Dough Process.

title: EiE Kindergarten: Programming Robots to Recycle
category: YES - EiE (Engineering is Elementary) Units
text: EiE Kindergarten: Programming Robots to Recycle is a EiE (Engineering is Elementary) Units unit from the Museum of Science, Boston. Students use programming skills to clean up a park and keep trash out of the landfill.

title: Designing Plant Packages
category: YES - EiE (Engineering is Elementary) Units
text: Designing Plant Packages is a EiE (Engineering is Elementary) Units unit from the Museum of Science, Boston. Students engineer a package to keep a plant healthy and whole during shipping.

title: Designing Solar Ovens
category: YES - EiE (Engineering is Elementary) Units
text: Designing Solar Ovens is a EiE (Engineering is Elementary) Units unit from the Museum of Science, Boston. Students learn about thermal energy transfer, collect data about insulation, and then engineer solar ovens.

title: Designing Windmills
category: YES - EiE (Engineering is Elementary) Units
text: Designing Windmills is a EiE (Engineering is Elementary) Units unit from the Museum of Science, Boston. Students explore the forces of wind and weather and engineer blades for a windmill that can lift weights.

title: Evaluating a Landscape
category: YES - EiE (Engineering is Elementary) Units
text: Evaluating a Landscape is a EiE (Engineering is Elementary) Units unit from the Museum of Science, Boston. Students explore landforms and erosion and propose the best place for a model suspension bridge. Aligned MA STE standard(s) via related exhibits: MS-LS2-2, MS-LS4-1. Related museum exhibits: New England Habitats, Natural Mysteries.

title: Improving a Play Dough Process
category: YES - EiE (Engineering is Elementary) Units
text: Improving a Play Dough Process is a EiE (Engineering is Elementary) Units unit from the Museum of Science, Boston. Students explore solids and liquids and develop a process for producing play dough.

title: Engineering Parachutes: Environmental Careers Exploration
category: YES - Career Explorations
text: Engineering Parachutes: Environmental Careers Exploration is a YES Career Exploration from the Museum of Science, Boston. Youth explore six roles: aeronautical engineer, documentary filmmaker, environmental planner, forest ecologist, pilot, and science communicator.

title: Engineering Rescue Shuttles: Disaster Recovery Careers Exploration
category: YES - Career Explorations
text: Engineering Rescue Shuttles: Disaster Recovery Careers Exploration is a YES Career Exploration from the Museum of Science, Boston. Youth explore six roles: aeronautical engineer, drone operator, firefighter, graphic designer, power plant operator, and real estate professional.

title: Engineering Antivirals: Health Careers Exploration
category: YES - Career Explorations
text: Engineering Antivirals: Health Careers Exploration is a YES Career Exploration from the Museum of Science, Boston. Youth explore six roles: biomedical engineer, health data analyst, health journalist, medical logistics director, nurse, and researcher.

title: Engineering Upcycled Toy Vehicles: Product Design Careers Exploration
category: YES - Career Explorations
text: Engineering Upcycled Toy Vehicles: Product Design Careers Exploration is a YES Career Exploration from the Museum of Science, Boston. Youth explore six careers connected to the product design theme of the engineering challenge: child development specialist, market researcher, mechanical engineer, packaging engineer, sustainability consultant, and theme park designer.

title: The Art of Illusion
category: Museum of Science Exhibit
text: The Art of Illusion is an exhibit at the Museum of Science, Boston. Explores how light reflects, refracts, and is processed visually by the eye and brain to shape visual perception. From the Museum of Science website: Discover how your brain interprets — and misinterprets — the world through illusions, hands-on displays, and works of art that challenge what you think you see. Matched YES learning activity: Engineering Vision Extenders. Primary MA STE standard: MS-PS4-2.

title: Innovation: Earth
category: Museum of Science Exhibit
text: Innovation: Earth is an exhibit at the Museum of Science, Boston. Examines emergent green technologies and sustainable engineering solutions designed to minimize human environmental impact. From the Museum of Science website: Explore emergent green technologies in the Museum’s brand-new immersive, interactive exhibit that helps us imagine the ways we’ll live, move, eat, and work in the future. Matched YES learning activity: Engineering Vertical Farms / Engineering Eco-friendly Slippers. Primary MA STE standard: MS-ESS3-4.

title: Gaia Globe
category: Museum of Science Exhibit
text: Gaia Globe is an exhibit at the Museum of Science, Boston. Uses detailed NASA satellite imagery on a floating 3D sphere to analyze Earth system dynamics and global climate patterns. From the Museum of Science website: View our planet on a grand scale, floating in three dimensions, when you gaze at UK artist Luke Jerram's Gaia artwork featuring detailed NASA imagery of the Earth's surface! Matched YES learning activity: Heatwave Visualizations (YES CS Module). Primary MA STE standard: MS-ESS3-2.

title: Exploring AI: Making the Invisible Visible
category: Museum of Science Exhibit
text: Exploring AI: Making the Invisible Visible is an exhibit at the Museum of Science, Boston. Demonstrates artificial intelligence, machine learning image classification, computer vision, and robotics interactions. From the Museum of Science website: Immerse yourself in AI as you observe real robots, create AI artwork, and experiment with a model that can “see.” Discover how AI is being applied, and consider its impact. Matched YES learning activity: Photo Classification (YES CS Module). Primary MA STE standard: MS-CS-1.

title: Hall of Human Life
category: Museum of Science Exhibit
text: Hall of Human Life is an exhibit at the Museum of Science, Boston. Investigates human biology, health technologies, organ system interactions, and biomedical engineering interventions. From the Museum of Science website: Explore what it means to be human in a time of rapid change. How are we transforming our world, and how is it changing our biology today and across generations? Matched YES learning activity: Engineering Bandages / Engineering Antivirals. Primary MA STE standard: MS-LS1-3.

title: Arctic Adventure: Exploring with Technology
category: Museum of Science Exhibit
text: Arctic Adventure: Exploring with Technology is an exhibit at the Museum of Science, Boston. Uses ground-penetrating radar, drones, and sensors to navigate extreme arctic environments and mitigate natural hazard risks. From the Museum of Science website: Fly a virtual drone to find an Arctic fox, traverse a glacier using ground-penetrating radar, and more in this immersive experience. Matched YES learning activity: Engineering an Avalanche Protection System. Primary MA STE standard: MS-ESS3-2.

title: Engineering Design Workshop
category: Museum of Science Exhibit
text: Engineering Design Workshop is an exhibit at the Museum of Science, Boston. Provides a hands-on maker studio where visitors define criteria, build prototypes, and test solutions to engineering challenges. From the Museum of Science website: Design, build, and test solutions! Discover the many ways engineers approach problem solving in surprising areas of our everyday lives. Matched YES learning activity: Engineering Earthquake-Resistant Buildings (All YES Units). Primary MA STE standard: MS-ETS1-2.

title: Colossal Fossil: Triceratops Cliff
category: Museum of Science Exhibit
text: Colossal Fossil: Triceratops Cliff is an exhibit at the Museum of Science, Boston. Examines a 65-million-year-old fossil to understand geological time scales and prehistoric organism structure. From the Museum of Science website: Get an up-close view of one of the world's rarest paleontological finds, a nearly complete 65-million-year-old fossil discovered in the Dakota Badlands in 2004. No matching YES activity (a curriculum gap), but it aligns with MA STE content standards. Primary MA STE standard: MS-ESS1-4.

title: Dinosaurs: Modeling the Mesozoic
category: Museum of Science Exhibit
text: Dinosaurs: Modeling the Mesozoic is an exhibit at the Museum of Science, Boston. Analyzes fossil evidence and life-size models to understand how paleontologists reconstruct ancient ecosystems. From the Museum of Science website: Check out fossils and life-size models to learn how paleontologists compile evidence and change the way we view these extinct animals. No matching YES activity (a curriculum gap), but it aligns with MA STE content standards. Primary MA STE standard: 4-ESS1-1.

title: Yawkey Gallery on the Charles River
category: Museum of Science Exhibit
text: Yawkey Gallery on the Charles River is an exhibit at the Museum of Science, Boston. Explores the connection between natural aquatic habitats and engineered urban infrastructure along the Charles River. From the Museum of Science website: Looking out over the Charles River, observe and explore the connections between natural habitats and engineered designs. Matched YES learning activity: Engineering Plastic Filters / Engineering Trash Collectors. Primary MA STE standard: MS-ESS3-3.

title: Theater of Electricity
category: Museum of Science Exhibit
text: Theater of Electricity is an exhibit at the Museum of Science, Boston. Features world's largest Van de Graaff generator demonstrating electrostatic forces, electric fields, and high-voltage lightning physics. From the Museum of Science website: Explore lightning and storm safety as the world's largest air-insulated Van de Graaff generator hurls indoor bolts. Matched YES learning activity: Engineering Nightlights / Light Sensors Module. Primary MA STE standard: MS-PS2-3.

title: Mathematica: A World of Numbers
category: Museum of Science Exhibit
text: Mathematica: A World of Numbers is an exhibit at the Museum of Science, Boston. Interactive kinetic displays designed by Charles & Ray Eames demonstrating mathematical models, geometry, and probability. From the Museum of Science website: Enjoy the wonder of mathematics and the beauty of post-modern design in this exhibit originally created by Charles and Ray Eames. Matched YES learning activity: Bounce Height Measurements (YES CS Module). Primary MA STE standard: MS-CS-2.

title: Math Moves!: Ratio & Proportion
category: Museum of Science Exhibit
text: Math Moves!: Ratio & Proportion is an exhibit at the Museum of Science, Boston. Immersive physical exhibits where visitors use full-body actions to investigate ratios, proportions, scale, and graphical motion data. From the Museum of Science website: Enjoy the wonder of mathematics and the beauty of post-modern design in this exhibit originally created by Charles and Ray Eames. Matched YES learning activity: Bounce Height Measurements (YES CS Module). Primary MA STE standard: MS-ETS1-7(MA).

title: Science in the Park
category: Museum of Science Exhibit
text: Science in the Park is an exhibit at the Museum of Science, Boston. Uses familiar playground equipment to explore forces, mechanical advantage, levers, momentum, and simple machines. From the Museum of Science website: Run, jump, and use familiar objects to investigate the pushes and pulls of everyday life. Matched YES learning activity: Wee Engineer: Wrecking Balls / Engineering Parachutes. Primary MA STE standard: MS-PS2-2.

title: Nanotechnology
category: Museum of Science Exhibit
text: Nanotechnology is an exhibit at the Museum of Science, Boston. title: Massachusetts STE Curriculum Framework objectives
category: MA STE Standards
text: Emphasizing Conceptual Understanding & Application: Shifting instruction from passive recall toward active investigation, engineering design prototyping, and real-world problem-solving. Integrating Core Ideas with Practices: Seamlessly blending core disciplinary knowledge across physical, life, and Earth/space sciences with Science and Engineering Practices (SEPs). Establishing Coherent Learning Progressions: Developing continuous, age-appropriate STEM progressions from early childhood through middle and high school. Elevating Technological & Engineering Literacy: Positioning Technology/Engineering as an essential academic discipline to build computational and design thinking. Fostering Career Readiness & Global Civic Engagement: Equipping students with data literacy, critical analysis skills, and problem-solving habits for post-secondary success.
